steps.body: The marks must be EQUALLY spaced — every gap of ten looks the same width, or the line starts telling lies about distance.
steps.narration: The marks must be EQUALLY spaced — every gap of ten looks the same width, or the line starts telling lies about distance.

widget.prompt: Trust the equal gaps: from 30, three equal ten-hops.

commonLandings.feedback: Three one-steps — equal gaps of TEN are what this line promises.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10, going forward. From 30, 3 hops land on 60.
widget.successFeedback: 60 — three identical gaps, three identical tens, one honest line.

predict.prompt: A line squeezes the gap between 40 and 50 smaller than the others. Trustworthy?
predict.reveal: A squeezed gap makes ten units look like five — the picture would contradict the values.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2l spacing.
invariants: Position on the line IS the number: equal jumps cover equal amounts, and a journey's landing depends only on start, jump size, and direction for g2l spacing.
misconceptions: Treating marks as decoration — unequal spacing, jumps of the wrong size, or reading a start mark as a landing.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Which change — start, jump size, or direction — would move the landing, and which would leave it alone?

widget.prompt: One line has marks at 20, 30, 40, 50. Another has marks at 20, 25, 40, 50. Which line is drawn correctly?

options.label: The second — more marks is better
options.feedback: Its gaps jump 5, then 15, then 10 — unequal gaps stretch and squash the numbers they hold.

options.label: Both — marks can sit anywhere
options.feedback: Marks carry meaning through their spacing; unequal gaps make equal distances LOOK different.

options.label: Neither — lines need to start at zero
options.feedback: A line may start anywhere it likes; what it owes you is equal spacing, not a zero.

options.label: The first — its gaps are all equal
options.feedback: Correct — 20, 30, 40, 50 steps by ten every time; equal gaps are what make a number line honest.

steps.body: Transfer the equal-spacing rule to a line whose marks are five apart.

widget.prompt: Use equal five-hops: start at 25 and make four hops to 45.

commonLandings.feedback: That is four one-steps, not four equal five-hops. Keep each gap the same size.

widget.missFeedback: Each equal gap is 5. From 25, four equal hops land on 45.
widget.successFeedback: 45 — four matching gaps of 5. Equal amounts received equal room on the line.

widget.prompt: A line is marked 0, 10, 20, 30. Where would 5 sit?

options.label: Directly on the 10 mark
options.feedback: 10 is the next labeled mark. The number 5 is halfway from 0 to that mark.

options.label: Halfway between the 0 and 10 marks
options.feedback: Correct — 5 is equally far from 0 and 10, so it is halfway across the first equal gap.

options.label: Halfway between the 10 and 20 marks
options.feedback: That position is 15. The number 5 belongs in the first gap, between 0 and 10.

options.label: To the right of the 30 mark
options.feedback: 5 is smaller than 30, so it belongs near the beginning of this number line.
